lines: Market is fully open for the last night: quick lines to Harbour and Hillside.
Mina is waiting at Market for a lift to Old Town.
Not everyone will make it home on time.
nightCard.footnote: The care home at Riverside is giving away its old railway photos, until ten past.

platform.headline: The last train on the Northline.
platform.coach: One question tonight. Then one last promise.

passengers.name: Wen
passengers.platform: Eighty tonight. The nurse is keeping him up for the cake until twenty past.
passengers.ask: He won't know it's his birthday. But I will. That's the deal we made years ago.

onTime.line: He blew out one candle. Then he said her name, clear as anything.
onTime.logLine: He blew out one candle, and said her name.

late.line: The cake was in the fridge. She sang to him anyway, quietly, while he slept.

notReached.line: She called. The nurse held the phone to his ear for the whole song.

passengers.name: Agnes
passengers.platform: Riding once more to say goodbye. The harbour lights a bonfire for the old line at half past.
passengers.ask: Fifty years on this line. I met my husband on the 23:40. Oh, they've moved the bonfire to twenty to, for the tide.

onTime.line: She stood by the bonfire and threw in her old season ticket.

late.line: The bonfire had burned down to embers. She warmed her hands on it anyway.

notReached.line: She watched the harbour glow from the train window, from far off.

passengers.name: Priya
passengers.platform: Last ride home. I'm busking the Old Town platform for the last train through.
passengers.ask: The song I wrote on your train. It's called Northline. Obviously.

onTime.line: She played Northline as you pulled out. You heard it through the window.

late.line: She played to an empty platform. Then the station lights went off, one by one.

notReached.line: She played Northline on your train instead, for whoever was still aboard.

passengers.name: Tomás
passengers.platform: Party loaves are in the oven. I'm on at twenty-five past.
passengers.ask: A new bakery's asked me to start Monday. Days. I'll see the sun.

onTime.line: He took the party loaves out at the stroke of one. The manager shook his hand.

late.line: They'd iced the party loaves without him. He did the last tray anyway.

notReached.line: He missed the party bake. He laughed about it, eventually.

passengers.name: Mina
passengers.platform: Can you pick me up at Market? Covering a shift at the Old Town clinic. Twenty to.
passengers.ask: I did a year at the Riverside home. Wen's dad called me “the tall one”. I'm not tall.

onTime.line: She was in her scrubs before handover finished. “Quiet night,” they said. It never is.

late.line: The day nurse stayed on for her and said nothing. That was worse.

notReached.line: A taxi on her own money. Beans until payday.

variants.platform: Last shift. Twenty-five past, then that's me done.

onTime.line: He did his last shift right. The manager shook his hand anyway.

variants.platform: He rang from the other side. He's wearing the scarf. Now, the bonfire's at half past.
He was asleep by twenty past last night. Quarter past, the nurse says. Please.
Not busking tonight. Mum's waiting up for me in Hillside, till twenty past. Don't ask about Thursday.
variants.planQuote: Mum's waiting up till twenty past.
variants.ask: I'll write another song. Not tonight. Tonight I want my mum's sofa.

onTime.line: Her mum had the kettle on. Neither of them mentioned the gig, and that was the kindest thing.

late.line: Her mum had gone to bed, but left the hall light on.

notReached.line: She walked up the hill in the dark with the guitar on her back.

coach.text: Tonight is Wen's dad's eightieth. You promised {promised}. Click a glowing station to start.
Three is the most anyone can do tonight, and every way to get three leaves Wen waiting. Saving her costs someone else.
You promised {promised}. On this route, they won't make it.
Two home. {waiting} would wait. Is it worth it? Only you can say.

logbook.tomorrow: The Northline is closed. The station lights go off, one by one.
